name: WPSDDC Info Vault
author: Didac Soria

sections.description:
Review content information and images directly in WordPress content lists. Keep shared notes and structured editorial checklists in the sidebar of the Classic or Block Editor.

Choose which public content types use Info Vault. All types start disabled. Existing 1.0.0 records are preserved when you update.

  • An Info column shows the native publication status, content ID, manual completion, shared notes and saved workflow sections.
  • An Images column shows the featured image and up to six additional local image previews. Existing image columns are respected.
  • Edit a shared note and a general checklist directly in the native editor sidebar, with an explicit Save Info Vault button.
  • Organize manual tasks under Register, Options, Marketing and SEO. Each web team chooses its own labels.
  • Define optional site templates for the four sections. Templates prefill sections that have never been saved; existing saved sections are unchanged.
  • Use the full record editor to work without JavaScript.
  • A stale form cannot silently overwrite a newer save. Failed sidebar saves keep your typed text available.

The controls follow your WordPress administration color scheme and adapt to narrow screens. Native Screen Options and mobile list-row controls remain available. A single local WPSDDC menu groups active collection plugins; no other WPSDDC plugin or HQ installation is required.

These are manual editorial tasks, not an automatic SEO audit or a ranking score. The plugin does not alter content, public SEO metadata, search-engine indexing or another plugin’s settings. No external service, telemetry, public shortcode or frontend asset is added.

WPSDDC identifies StudioDDC’s independent plugin collection. This plugin is not affiliated with or endorsed by the WordPress Foundation or Automattic.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WPSDDC Info Vault.
  2. Open WPSDDC > Info Vault, select the public content types you need and save.
  3. Optionally enter starting lists for Register, Options, Marketing and SEO.
  4. Save a content draft, open its Info Vault sidebar panel, edit your notes and tasks, and select Save Info Vault.
  5. Review saved information and image previews from the native content list. Use Screen Options to show or hide columns.
sections.faq:
Who can read and edit a record?

People who can edit the corresponding content, using its normal WordPress permissions. Notes and checklists are shared administrative information. They are not displayed on the public website or added to public content REST responses. Storage is not encrypted against database or server administrators.

Does Update or autosave save the sidebar?

No. Select Save Info Vault explicitly. This keeps content saves and editorial records independent. If another window saved a newer revision, reload before saving again; your unsaved text remains in the current panel. Use the full editor link if JavaScript is unavailable.

What can I put in a checklist?

Up to 20 distinct plain-text items of 120 characters each, per section. The general checklist and each of the four workflow sections have their own completion flags. Reordering unchanged labels preserves completion; renaming creates a new incomplete item. Save new or renamed items before marking them complete. The shared note supports up to 10,000 characters.

Do templates change existing records?

No. A site administrator can define starting text for each workflow section. It is offered only until that section has been saved for a content item. Changing a template does not rewrite saved content records. No automatic migration reads HQ settings or notes.

Which images are shown?

The plugin reads local WordPress attachment references from the featured image, supported Core image/gallery/media-text/cover blocks, classic image classes and gallery shortcodes. Image discovery considers at most 256 KiB of content, 100 blocks, six nesting levels and 25 candidate attachment IDs. Up to six additional previews are displayed; this is not a complete media inventory. External image URLs are not resolved or downloaded. Only image attachments the current user can read are shown.

Does it need paid SEO or language plugins?

No. Info Vault uses its own records and native WordPress permissions. It works without another SEO or language plugin. Polylang Free translations keep independent records for their separate WordPress content IDs. Existing SEO metadata is left unchanged. WooCommerce products can use the same editorial workflow; their native image column is retained and local gallery previews are appended. This does not provide a WooCommerce translation bridge or replace other plugins’ premium features.

Can it run next to HQ?

The two plugins have independent settings and storage. Enable an equivalent editorial workflow in one of them to avoid duplicate panels or Info columns. Installing this plugin does not import or change HQ data.

What happens when I disable or remove it?

Records and settings are retained. Disabling a content type retains its records. Records can also remain after related content is deleted, without an automatic cleanup job. Clear unwanted text explicitly while the content still exists.

Where are help and translations?

Open WPSDDC > Info Vault and the native Help tab for setup, data limits and support. English is the source language. Approved community language packs are supplied through WordPress.org when available. StudioDDC maintains a Spanish source catalog in the development repository; catalogs are excluded from the WordPress.org installable ZIP.

Support: English / Spanish. Following a support link opens the external site; no automatic support request is sent.
sections.changelog:
1.1.1

  • Refine checklist alignment, field spacing, Info card padding and image-preview layout.
  • Balance the full record editor and site workflow templates without changing saved data.
  • Verify WordPress 7.2 RC3 and PHP 8.6 compatibility, including native editor saves and administration icons.
  • Replace the gallery with six desktop screenshots using varied StudioDDC website photographs.

1.1.0

  • Add content-list information cards, featured image and bounded local image previews.
  • Add direct sidebar editing and explicit record saves in the Classic and Block Editors.
  • Add configurable Register, Options, Marketing and SEO sections and optional site templates.
  • Preserve existing 1.0.0 records, object permissions and atomic stale-write protection.
  • Improve responsive table layout and retain native mobile row controls and Screen Options.
  • Refresh English screenshots and centered StudioDDC banner artwork.

1.0.0

  • Initial WordPress.org release with shared editorial notes, checklists, explicit content type opt-ins and independent record saves.
